questions.q: Edit: 'He didn't went to the doctor yesterday.'
questions.a: 'went' → 'go' — after 'didn't' the verb returns to base; 'did' already carries the past. A wrong answer 'didn't goed' creates a new error instead of fixing the old.

questions.q: Edit: 'She was cooking dinner and eats it quickly.'
questions.a: 'eats' → 'ate' — tense drift; both actions share the past time-zone. A wrong answer changing 'was cooking' shows the student picks the wrong verb to fix.

questions.q: Edit: 'Look! The baby crawl towards the door.'
questions.a: 'crawl' → 'is crawling' — 'Look!' demands present continuous, and it needs the be-auxiliary. A wrong answer 'crawls' misses the marker entirely.
